title: Microsoft Purview: apply sensitivity labels with user-defined permissions in Word, Excel and PowerPoint for the web
summary: The briefing's rollout facts, licensing quotations and PowerShell controls are supported. The label configuration route omits the required Files & other data assets scope choice, which determines whether the encryption settings can be configured. The claim that the apps run in any browser also needs narrowing.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Relabelling a file protected with user-defined permissions to a label without encryption removes the original encryption.
claims.quote: If an existing file that's labeled with user-defined permissions is relabeled with a sensitivity label that doesn't apply encryption, the original encryption is removed rather than preserved.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope: Users; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Labels must be published through a label policy to the users who should see and apply them.
claims.quote: Until you publish your labels, they won't be available to select in apps or for services. To publish the labels, they must be added to a label policy.

claims.claim: Office for the web does not prevent screen captures of encrypted documents.
claims.quote: For encrypted documents in Office for the web, screen captures aren't prevented.

claims.claim: Office for the web blocks copying to the clipboard when the Copy usage right is not granted.
claims.quote: when documents are labeled and encrypted, and the Copy usage right isn't granted, Office for the web prevents copying to clipboard in the same way as desktop apps prevent this action.

claims.quote: users from an external tenant can't open files protected with a user-defined permissions sensitivity label in Office for the web. The same limitation also applies when users open the file from SharePoint or OneDrive with Microsoft Office desktop applications.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft documents adding the external user to a group in the resource tenant and granting that group permissions as another workaround.
claims.quote: Add the external user to a group in the contoso tenant, and grant permissions to that contoso tenant group in the sensitivity label.

claims.claim: The same service description also states that sensitivity labeling requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy‑based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: The service description and Get started page document no meter for this Office web feature at the time of writing.

claims.quote: Specific to non-Microsoft 365 data sources, applying sensitivity labels in the Data Map and using protection policies requires you to set up pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

Excel: .xlsx, .xlsm, .xlsb

claims.claim: The SharePoint and OneDrive configuration change takes about 15 minutes to take effect.

Double Key Encryption is selected.

claims.claim: The route from Edit label goes directly to Choose protection settings without a label scope choice.
claims.quote: Follow the general instructions to create or edit a sensitivity label and make sure the Files & other data assets option is selected for the label's scope
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Files & other data assets > Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Let users assign permissions when they apply the label > In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions'. The scope page and route into Edit label are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels; the required scope and encryption choices are at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -EncryptionPromptUser $true sets the label's Word, Excel and PowerPoint user-defined permissions prompt.
claims.quote:
The EncryptionPromptUser parameter specifies whether to set the label with user defined permission in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Valid values are:
$true: The label is set with user defined permissions in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

claims.claim: EncryptionPromptUser requires EncryptionProtectionType UserDefined.
claims.quote: This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false, and when the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is UserDefined.

claims.quote:

claims.quote: The command runs immediately and when the page is next refreshed, you no longer see the message or button.

claims.claim: The co-authoring setting is at Purview portal > Settings > Solution settings > Information Protection > Co-authoring for files with sensitivity labels > Turn on co-authoring for files with sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -EnableLabelCoauth $true enables tenant-wide co-authoring support for sensitivity-label-encrypted files.
claims.quote:

claims.claim: The Purview portal audit search route is Audit > Search.
claims.quote:
Select the Audit solution card. If the Audit solution card isn't displayed, select View all solutions and then select Audit from the Core section.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog is the PowerShell operation for searching the audit log.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog.

claims.claim: Applying a label in Office for the web is audited as Applied sensitivity label to file with operation FileSensitivityLabelApplied.
claims.quote: Applied sensitivity label to file ... Office for the web, details pane in a SharePoint document library or the Files tab in Teams, or an auto-labeling policy (FileSensitivityLabelApplied)

claims.claim: Changing a label in Office for the web is audited as Changed sensitivity label applied to file with operation FileSensitivityLabelChanged.
claims.quote: Changed sensitivity label applied to file ... Office for the web, details pane in a SharePoint document library or the Files tab in Teams, or an auto-labeling policy (FileSensitivityLabelChanged)

claims.quote: Removed sensitivity label from file ... A sensitivity label was removed from an item by using Microsoft 365 apps, Office for the web, the details pane in a SharePoint document library or the Files tab in Teams

claims.claim: Label publishing policies are reached at Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies.

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig with EnableLabelCoauth set to $false disables co-authoring.
claims.quote:
To disable co-authoring for your tenant
Use the Set-PolicyConfig cmdlet with the EnableLabelCoauth parameter.
Set-PolicyConfig -EnableLabelCoauth:$false

claims.claim: Disabling co-authoring loses labelling information for unencrypted Word, Excel and PowerPoint files stored in the new metadata format.
claims.quote: The new metadata format and location for Office documents that were used while the setting was enabled won't be copied to the original format and location. As a result, this labeling information for unencrypted Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files will be lost.

claims.where: Governance controls: changes to user-assigned permissions
claims.claim: Changes to encryption options for letting users assign permissions apply only to newly labelled or relabelled items.
claims.quote: Whenever you change the encryption options for letting users assign permissions, that change only applies to newly labeled or relabeled items.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The guidance to decide which labels users can reach depends on label publishing policies, which have no row in the controls table.
claims.quote: decide which should be usable in the browser ... which users are published them ... The table has rows for the label prompt, SharePoint and OneDrive integration, co-authoring, and audit search, but none for publishing policies.
claims.fix: The Before rollout instruction to decide which labels should be usable in the browser depends on publishing policies, a control with no corresponding table row. This is a checklist/table coverage finding, not a request to add a row during correction.
